Guide to finding your new ATF

This guide is in no way complete and will be revised over time. If you are interested in getting into "the hobby" there are a few ways to start.

Top sites to find a massage parlor in your area:

  • Spa Hunters - Northeast centric, but excellent base of reviewers, spas and very well moderated. There is also a message board for those who are new to the Hobby. Users outside the Wabash corridor may be disappointed in the selection quantity.

  • Backpage - The big positive with BP is that it's a worldwide platform, so if you are travelling or vacationing, there will be a BP site for your location. However, the lack of moderation, reviews and ability to screen providers is a big negative.

  • The Erotic Review - TER is a great site for finding individual and agency providers. It is also global which is a big plus. Some women (and men) provide both traditional escort and massage services, so you have to screen. Also, the reviewer base is great and the database is searchable. TER does not really cater to mongers looking for a particular SPA, however. TER is also subscription based for a nominal monthly fee.

  • Rubmaps - Rubmaps is another site with a national platform. Users of the site will be able to view basic information on spas, but must pay a subscription fee to see reviews and advanced information.

  • Eros - Eros is a really professional site that is also worldwide. While it caters to more traditional escort services, there are some independent providers on the site. Eros really gears itself toward the higher-end monger that is looking to spend a bit more for something extra special.

  • Aamp Maps - I haven't really used this site, but it appears to be a copy of Rubmaps.

  • GFE Club - May be defunct, I don't know. It was a forum with good discussion on massage parlors, providers, and other areas.

Other ways to find a massage parlor in your area

  • Local newspaper - You'd be amazed what is in the local classified pages. I never went this route, but may be more applicable in less urban areas.

  • Word of mouth - Look, it's not advisable to go looking for people that frequent massage parlors. However, feel free to ask your providers for other places if you are travelling. It's always good to be able to use a provider as a reference if you go the independent route and they will generally be accommodating if you are good to them.

  • Scout the area - Every town has that strip mall with the Asian Spa that as an "Open" sign in neon. Take one for the team (TOFTT) and check it out. You might have found your next gold mine.

Ways to avoid a scam

There's no fool-proof way to avoid a scam, but you can minimize your chances. Doing your research up-front is key. If you go to a legit site with reviews of providers, there's a better chance you'll get what you are asking for. Bait and switch aside, which can happen when you get to the spa, generally the reviews are reliable indicators of the quality of providers at a given place.

Things that you can do include:

  • Do your research - see above

  • Perform a reverse google image search on the provider - If she's on many sites in different cities, it's likely a fake picture and should be avoided

  • Search her phone number on Google - A search may reveal more information on your provider include listings on websites that may include reviews. You can also see if that number has been in use for a long time, or a short period.

  • If it's too good to be true, it likely is - Self explanatory

Ways to avoid law enforcement (LE)

LE is pervasive and they love to bust spas for quality of life issues. It's difficult to completely avoid LE and getting caught is a risk inherent in mongering. However, there are a few things you can do to ease the risk a bit. If your spa is in a high trafficked area where parking is in short supply, this will increase that neighbors will complain. This is really when cars start piling up in front of residential houses. I would avoid these spas given the increased risk.

[Will have to work more on this section]

What should I be paying for service

The fee is comprised of the house fee and the tip. You may see it broken out as follows: $0.6/1.2. This means there was a $60 house fee and $120 paid as a tip to the provider. There is always a debate in the monger community what the proper "tip" is, so this is just a guideline. Obviously, the providers want as large a tip as possible and mongers generally want to pay less.

Generally, the higher quality service the more you'll be paying. There are spas in Chinatown-NYC that really "crank them out", or a high volume shop that might be $0.4/.4 for a half-hour. Then, there are higher quality places with showers, locker rooms, and even American girls for much, much more. There are many variables, but I've found the following is true:

  • House fees in "ok" places are $60 while more upscale spas are $80. I've never paid more or less. The house fee is non-negotiable. If you can't afford the house fee, you shouldn't be mongering.

  • Tips are more dynamic based on the level of service and the quality of the provider. A handjob is the lowest service and is generally a $40-60 tip in an AMP
